sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, Kurt Kolstad produced an episode about trains, only trains, and nothing but trains,
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，库尔特·科尔斯特制作了一期关于火车的节目，纯粹是火车，只有火车，

sentences.en: featuring strange and amazing rail cars and routes from around the world.
sentences.zh: 其中介绍了来自世界各地的奇特惊艳的铁轨车辆与路线。

sentences.en: But he ran into a little bit of a problem.
sentences.zh: 但他遇到了一点小麻烦。

sentences.en: Fortunately, it was the good kind of problem.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，这是个美妙的麻烦。

sentences.en: I had way too many train stories for a single episode.
sentences.zh: 单凭一期节目，我的火车故事实在太多了。

sentences.en: And not just my ideas, but also ideas sent in by fans.
sentences.zh: 不仅有我的想法，还有粉丝们发来的创意。

sentences.en: And it was pretty clear from all the tweets and emails that you beautiful nerds would be down for a second round of train stories.
sentences.zh: 从所有的推文和邮件中很明显可以看出，你们这群可爱的极客们一定会喜欢第二波火车故事。

sentences.en: So here it is.
sentences.zh: 所以它来了。

sentences.en: Train set, track two.
sentences.zh: 列车就位，二号轨道。

sentences.en: All aboard.
sentences.zh: 请上车。

sentences.en: Greetings, passengers.
sentences.zh: 乘客们好。

sentences.en: This is your conductor speaking.
sentences.zh: 我是你们的列车长。

sentences.en: Our first stop today will be Wellington, New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的首站是新西兰惠灵顿。

sentences.en: This story starts not with a train, but with a photo of a train.
sentences.zh: 这个故事不是从一辆火车开始的，而是从一张火车的照片开始的。

sentences.en: When I was working on our previous episode about trains,
sentences.zh: 当我正在制作上一期关于火车的节目时，

sentences.en: I found this wonderful picture of this cable car in Wellington.
sentences.zh: 我发现了这张惠灵顿缆车的绝美照片。

sentences.en: And I decided to use it as a lead image on our website when we released that episode.
sentences.zh: 当我们在发布那一期节目时，我决定把它用作我们网站的头图。

sentences.en: Yes, I remember that one.
sentences.zh: 没错，我记得那一张。

sentences.en: It was this really lovely shot.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常可爱的镜头。

sentences.en: It's a red funicular climbing up a hill in a city with mountains in the background.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆红色的缆车，正爬上一座城市的小山，背景是群山。

sentences.en: And, you know, the funny thing was, we didn't actually talk about that funicular, did we?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有趣的是，我们实际上并没有讨论那个缆车，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, we didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，没有，我们没有。

sentences.en: I was just looking for, you know, the ultimate train picture.
sentences.zh: 我只是在寻找，你知道的，终极的火车照片。

sentences.en: Plus, I figured it's a funicular.
sentences.zh: 另外，我想这是一种缆车。

sentences.en: That's something you would enjoy.
sentences.zh: 那是你会喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: You know who didn't enjoy it?
sentences.zh: 你知道谁不喜欢吗？

sentences.en: New Zealanders.
sentences.zh: 新西兰人。

sentences.en: They were very polite about it, but it was clear that seeing an image
sentences.zh: 他们对此很有礼貌，但很明显，看到一张照片

sentences.en: had gotten more than a few Wellingtonians excited about their city being featured on the show.
sentences.zh: 让不少惠灵顿人对他们的城市登上节目感到兴奋不已。

sentences.en: So I started chatting with a friend who lives in Wellington.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始和一位住在惠灵顿的朋友聊天。

sentences.en: And, well, I'll just let her set the scene.
sentences.zh: 而且，好吧，我就让她来介绍一下背景吧。

sentences.en: One of the first things you notice when you move to Wellington is these funny little rails
sentences.zh: 当你搬到惠灵顿，最先注意到的事情之一就是这些有趣的小铁轨，

sentences.en: going up the hill as you drive along.
sentences.zh: 当你开车经过时，它们正顺着山坡往上延伸。

sentences.en: And you're like, well, what the heck is that?
sentences.zh: 你会想，这到底是什么鬼？

sentences.en: Is that an elevator?
sentences.zh: 那是一个电梯吗？

sentences.en: That's my friend and de facto New Zealand correspondent, Pepper.
sentences.zh: 那是我的朋友兼事实上的新西兰通讯员佩珀。

sentences.en: I'm Pepper Raccoon, and I'm an artist from Wellington, New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 我是佩珀·拉昆，我是来自新西兰惠灵顿的艺术家。

sentences.en: Her name is Pepper Raccoon?
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫佩珀·拉昆？

sentences.en: That is outstanding.
sentences.zh: 这太绝了。

sentences.en: I can see why you guys hit it off.
sentences.zh: 我能理解为什么你们俩能合得来。

sentences.en: And those rails that she's talking about, they're not just for that one main cable car.
sentences.zh: 她谈到的那些铁轨，不仅仅是那一条主要的缆车轨道。

sentences.en: There are a bunch of smaller private trains around the city, too.
sentences.zh: 这座城市周围还有许多较小的私人火车。

sentences.en: I think, honestly, Wellington is the best place to come for a tour of the best funiculars.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为惠灵顿是参观最佳缆车的绝佳去处。

sentences.en: It's a, yeah, it's a smorgasbord, really.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个，对，真的是一个大杂烩。

sentences.en: There's so many different ones, and they all look completely different.
sentences.zh: 有太多不同的种类，而且它们看起来完全不同。

sentences.en: And she explained to me that there are actually hundreds of local funiculars in Wellington.
sentences.zh: 她向我解释说，惠灵顿实际上有数百个本地缆车。

sentences.en: They range from, like, a fiberglass bucket on a single rail to, like, effectively a beautiful little room elevator
sentences.zh: 它们的范围从小巧的、装在单轨上的玻璃钢斗子，到实际上像是一个精美的小房间电梯，

sentences.en: that mimics the style of your home on a dual rail that gives it a much smoother and stabler ride.
sentences.zh: 它模仿你家的风格，安装在双轨上，能带来更平稳、更稳定的乘坐体验。

sentences.en: So it's like, yeah, you can go real fancy.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是，对，你可以弄得很豪华。

sentences.en: So Wellington is now becoming, like, the first city of my heart because it has tons of funiculars,
sentences.zh: 因此，惠灵顿现在成了我心中的第一城市，因为它有大量的缆车，

sentences.en: which, as we all know, are the greatest form of transportation.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，缆车是最好的交通工具。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: But the question still remains, why are there so many funiculars in Wellington?
sentences.zh: 但问题依然存在，为什么惠灵顿会有这么多的缆车？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And it's not so much that the city itself as a public entity needs them.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为城市本身作为公共实体需要它们。

sentences.en: It's that all of these homeowners do.
sentences.zh: 而是因为所有这些房主都需要。

sentences.en: Because Wellington is this small coastal city, and it's crammed in between the water and all these craggy hills.
sentences.zh: 因为惠灵顿是一个小型的沿海城市，它被挤在水面和所有这些崎岖的山丘之间。

sentences.en: In terms of the topography, it's just a nightmare of, like, crumbling cliffs.
sentences.zh: 就地形而言，这里简直就是一片悬崖崩塌的噩梦。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that we ran out of space.
sentences.zh: 所以我们用尽空间也就合情合理了。

sentences.en: And so houses kind of ended up on cliffs and on very steep hills.
sentences.zh: 因此，房屋最终最终建在了悬崖上和非常陡峭的山丘上。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's good.
sentences.zh: 对，这挺好。

sentences.en: It's also, like, an insane place, though, because of the topography.
sentences.zh: 不过，由于地形原因，这也像是一个疯狂的地方。

sentences.en: So a lot of things don't make sense here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里很多事情都说不通。

sentences.en: Or rather, they make sense here but sound weird to everybody else.
sentences.zh: 或者说，在这里说得通，但在其他人听来却很奇怪。

sentences.en: And so Wellington is actually one of the most densely populated cities in New Zealand because there's so little flatland to build on.
sentences.zh: 因此，惠灵顿实际上是新西兰人口最稠密的城市之一，因为可供建造的平地太少了。

sentences.en: And people have decided to move up and out of the densely packed city and live on these steep slopes, which otherwise might not get built on.
sentences.zh: 人们决定搬到人口稠密的城市上方和外围，住在这些陡峭的山坡上，否则这些地方可能不会被开发。

sentences.en: And this approach has upsides and it has downsides.
sentences.zh: 这种方法既有好处，也有坏处。

sentences.en: So those homes on the coast have incredible views.
sentences.zh: 所以海边的那些房子拥有令人难以置信的视野。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, moving into them means you have to hire a helicopter.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，搬进去意味着你必须租一架直升机。

sentences.en: So heaven forbid you buy a new sofa.
sentences.zh: 所以千万别买新沙发。

sentences.en: Like, I couldn't imagine buying new furniture after having moved in and being like, well, I guess we have to call the helicopter again.
sentences.zh: 比如，我无法想象搬进去之后再买新家具，然后想，好吧，我想我们又得叫直升机了。

sentences.en: Like, that sucks.
sentences.zh: 这感觉太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But because most people, of course, can't hire a helicopter every time they want to go to the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 但因为大多数人当然不能每次想去超市时都租一架直升机。

sentences.en: And the only way to get up to some of those houses was a set of stairs, if you're lucky.
sentences.zh: 如果你运气好，去其中一些房子的唯一方法就是一组楼梯。

sentences.en: And for some houses, it's literally just the funicular.
sentences.zh: 对于某些房子来说，字面意思就是只有缆车。

sentences.en: So you can get stuck there.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会被困在那里。

sentences.en: Your funicular can break down and you can just not be able to go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你的缆车可能会坏掉，然后你就哪儿也去不了了。

sentences.en: And they do.
sentences.zh: 它们确实会。

sentences.en: Yeah, and they do break down and they can be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 对，它们确实会坏掉，而且可能很危险。

sentences.en: Someone did die due to a funicular related incident before there was regulations around them.
sentences.zh: 在对缆车进行监管之前，确实有人因缆车相关的事故而丧生。

sentences.en: And so the government had to institute a warrant of fitness on funiculars.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府不得不对缆车实施适航证制度。

sentences.en: But it's really expensive.
sentences.zh: 但这真的很贵。

sentences.en: When the maintenance costs are so expensive and you have to keep the piles, you know, stable and hire inspectors and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 当维护成本如此高昂，你必须保持桩基（你知道的）稳定并聘请检查员以及所有这些事情时。

sentences.en: And so that cost becomes a pretty big deal because these trains aren't being run by the city.
sentences.zh: 所以这笔费用成了一个相当大的问题，因为这些火车不是由城市运营的。

sentences.en: They're owned, operated and maintained by individuals or small groups of homeowners.
sentences.zh: 它们是由个人或小群业主拥有、运营和维护的。

sentences.en: Some people have teamed up.
sentences.zh: 有些人组成了团队。

sentences.en: So there'll be three or four houses on the same funicular track.
sentences.zh: 所以会有三四栋房子共用同一条缆车轨道。

sentences.en: And so you just share it.
sentences.zh: 然后你们就共享它。

sentences.en: And that seems really sensible.
sentences.zh: 这看起来真的很明智。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people don't get fancy with their funiculars either.
sentences.zh: 因此，很多人也没有把他们的缆车弄得太花哨。

sentences.en: They just need something to get them tuned from home safely, something they can afford.
sentences.zh: 他们只是需要某种能安全带他们往返于家中的工具，一种他们负担得起的东西。

sentences.en: But even the safety part is a little bit optional.
sentences.zh: 但甚至连安全部分也是有点可选的。

sentences.en: New Zealanders also have this really dangerous and kind of entertaining, seems whimsical, but also kind of terrible philosophy called she'll be right.
sentences.zh: 新西兰人还有这种非常危险、有点有趣、看起来异想天开但又有点糟糕的哲学，叫做“一切都会好起来的”（she'll be right）。

sentences.en: Which is just build something.
sentences.zh: 也就是随便造点东西。

sentences.en: Don't worry too much about it.
sentences.zh: 不用太担心。

sentences.en: She'll be right.
sentences.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I think a lot of the funiculars that existed before the warrant of fitness might have been on that kind of spectrum.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我认为在颁发适航证之前存在的许多缆车可能都处于这种范畴。

sentences.en: Because it's all funiculars and games until someone gets hurt.
sentences.zh: 因为这本是缆车与游戏，直到有人受伤。

sentences.en: But despite them being janky and unpredictable, she absolutely wants to ride on a private funicular.
sentences.zh: 但尽管它们破旧且不可预测，她绝对还是想坐一次私人缆车。

sentences.en: OK, I've been on the cable car.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我坐过缆车。

sentences.en: I have never been on a personal funicular.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有坐过个人缆车。

sentences.en: And the one person that I talked to that was willing to let me ride on their funicular, their funicular was broken, which I have been told is very common.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的唯一一个愿意让我坐他们缆车的人，他们的缆车坏了，据说这很常见。

sentences.en: Next stop will be Goat Canyon, California.
sentences.zh: 下一站将是加利福尼亚州的山羊峡谷。

sentences.en: Please be advised that the track beyond this point is abandoned.
sentences.zh: 请注意，此点之后的铁轨已被废弃。

sentences.en: Goat Canyon is situated in a beautiful stretch of desert east of San Diego, California.
sentences.zh: 山羊峡谷坐落在加利福尼亚州圣迭戈以东一片美丽的沙漠中。

sentences.en: And it's a great place to ride the rails.
sentences.zh: 这是铁轨骑行的好去处。

sentences.en: Oh, so now we got to move some shit out of the way here.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以现在我们得把一些破烂从这里移开。

sentences.en: OK, so what am I looking at here?
sentences.zh: 好的，那我在这里看到的是什么？

sentences.en: Basically, like a really low tech go-kart that runs on rails instead of roads.
sentences.zh: 基本上就像一个在铁轨上行驶而不是在公路上行驶的低技术卡丁车。

sentences.en: So it's this bare-bones plywood platform with four wheels attached and a couple of bucket seats and a motor.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个简陋的胶合板平台，连接着四个轮子、几个斗式座位和一个发动机。

sentences.en: And beyond that, just a cooler strap between them for beers and sandwiches and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，中间还绑着一个冷却箱，用来装啤酒、三明治之类东西。

sentences.en: And in this particular video, you've got two brothers who are out there, one who built the thing and one who's recording their adventure.
sentences.zh: 在这段特定的视频中，有两个兄弟在那里，一个建造了这个东西，另一个在记录他们的冒险。

sentences.en: And they're just taking to these abandoned rails.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在这些废弃的铁轨上行驶。

sentences.en: I cannot believe we're doing this.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信我们正在这样做。

sentences.en: So clearly this is an abandoned set of tracks.
sentences.zh: 很明显这是一套废弃的铁轨。

sentences.en: So where are they going?
sentences.zh: 那么他们要去哪里？

sentences.en: They're heading up to see the Goat Canyon Trestle Bridge, which was built nearly 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 他们正前往参观山羊峡谷栈桥桥，该桥建于近100年前。

sentences.en: And it's the largest wood trestle bridge in the world.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最大的木结构栈桥。

sentences.en: Largest per trestle.
sentences.zh: 按栈桥计算是最大的。

sentences.en: So it's this massive and daunting structure that's around 750 feet long and 200 feet high.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个庞大而令人望而生畏的结构，长约750英尺，高200英尺。

sentences.en: But like if you're on rails and you're going 20 miles an hour and it's an abandoned track and maybe some other daredevil is also going 20 miles an hour,
sentences.zh: 但如果你在铁轨上，以每小时20英里的速度行驶，这是一条废弃的铁轨，也许另一个勇敢者也以每小时20英里的速度行驶，

sentences.en: hopefully in the same direction, maybe not in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 希望是同一个方向，也许不是同一个方向。

sentences.en: I mean, like what happens?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So the good thing is these carts don't weigh a lot, so they don't have a ton of mass, which means they can stop relatively quickly if you see an obstacle.
sentences.zh: 所以好消息是这些推车不是很重，所以它们没有那么大的质量，这意味着如果你看到障碍物，它们可以相对较快地停下来。

sentences.en: Plus, people who regularly ride these stretches, they know more or less what to expect.
sentences.zh: 另外，经常骑这些路段的人多多少少知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: People like Gabe Emerson, a tinkerer from Alaska who has built a few rail carts over the years.
sentences.zh: 像加布·爱默生这样的人，来自阿拉斯加的修补匠，这些年来建造了几个轨道车。

sentences.en: In this video, I'm going to try to make a railroad speeder or homemade rail cart.
sentences.zh: 在这段视频中，我要试着做一个铁路轨道车或自制轨道车。

sentences.en: Now, I've had a couple of these in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，我过去有过几个这样的东西。

sentences.en: If you've seen my prior videos, you may have seen the horrible antique metal one, and you've probably seen my horrible plastic one that kept derailing constantly.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过我之前的视频，你可能看过那个糟糕的古董金属车，你可能也看过我那个经常脱轨的糟糕塑料车。

sentences.en: My hope here is to make one that actually stays on the track and that I can take out to some abandoned railroads for a bit of fun.
sentences.zh: 我这里的希望是做一个真正能留在铁轨上并且我可以带到一些废弃铁路上玩乐的东西。

sentences.en: And true to the title of his video channel, Save It For Parts, Gabe is using pieces he's recycling from these previous builds,
sentences.zh: 正如他的视频频道名称“留作零件”（Save It For Parts）一样，加布正在使用他从这些以前的构筑中回收的零件，

sentences.en: like a pedal-powered rail bike that he built and a speeder that was kind of like this one.
sentences.zh: 比如他建造的脚踏式铁轨自行车和有点像这个的速度车。

sentences.en: But this time he added a new motor and a gas pedal.
sentences.zh: 但这次他增加了一个新电机和一个油门踏板。

sentences.en: And of course, he doesn't need a steering wheel because it's on train tracks with no turns.
sentences.zh: 当然，他不需要方向盘，因为它是在没有转弯的火车轨道上。

sentences.en: And in the end, this creation worked, more or less.
sentences.zh: 最后，这个发明多多少少成功了。

sentences.en: My chain keeps jumping off.
sentences.zh: 我的链条一直在跳脱。

sentences.en: I need like a tensioner or something on here.
sentences.zh: 我需要在这里装个张紧器之类的东西。

sentences.en: Actually, I've lost a nut from my finally, finally engineered gearing system.
sentences.zh: 其实，我精细设计的齿轮系统丢了一个螺母。

sentences.en: So that's why the chain keeps popping off.
sentences.zh: 这就是链条老是脱落的原因。

sentences.en: Oh, geez, here come the parkies.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，公园巡警来了。

sentences.en: So what he's referring to here are these park cops who happen to be passing by and apparently driving a little weird DIY vehicle at slow speeds down an abandoned set of railroad tracks isn't something they're used to ticketing.
sentences.zh: 所以他这里指的是这些刚好路过的公园警察，显然，驾驶一辆奇怪的小型DIY交通工具以低速在废弃的铁路上行驶并不是他们习惯开罚单的事情。

sentences.en: In any case, after that, Gabe reflected on his work and called it a day.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，在那之后，加布反思了他的工作并收工了。

sentences.en: This thing may not be fast, but at least it's ugly.
sentences.zh: 这个东西可能不快，但至少它很丑。

sentences.en: Are you allowed to do that?
sentences.zh: 你被允许这样做吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: No, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对没有。

sentences.en: In general, yeah, no.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，对，也不是。

sentences.en: But there are some legal DIY rail riding options for people who want to, you know, stay above board or just don't want to build their own carts.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些想，你知道的，遵纪守法，或者只是不想自己造车的，有一些合法的DIY铁轨骑行选择。

sentences.en: OK, so so like what?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那……那比如呢？

sentences.en: Well, there's this place up in northern California, for example, near Fort Bragg called Rail Bikes,
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如说加州北部有一个地方，靠近布拉格堡，叫做“铁轨单车”，

sentences.en: and they rent out four wheeled two seat vehicles that use a combination of electricity and pedal power.
sentences.zh: 他们出租结合了电力和脚踏动力的四轮双座车。

sentences.en: For a long time, there was this 40 mile active rail line that ran between Fort Bragg and Willits.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，有一条40英里长的活跃铁路线在布拉格堡和威利茨之间运行。

sentences.en: But then about a decade ago, this key tunnel along the route collapsed and basically cut the line in two.
sentences.zh: 但大约十年前，这条路线上的一个关键隧道坍塌了，基本上把这条线路截成了两段。

sentences.en: So people on both sides decided to spin up these shorter rail options like this to make the best of a bad situation.
sentences.zh: 因此，两边的人决定推出这些较短的铁轨选择，以此来充分利用糟糕的局面。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Well, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这倒挺合理。

sentences.en: I mean, they're they're there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们就在那儿。

sentences.en: Why not use them if they can't be used by trains?
sentences.zh: 既然火车不能用了，为什么不用它们呢？

sentences.en: Let's use them for something else.
sentences.zh: 我们把它用在别的地方吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's been maintained until quite recently, making for a safer ride.
sentences.zh: 它直到最近才得到维护，让骑行更安全。

sentences.en: And there's all this existing rail infrastructure already in place.
sentences.zh: 而且所有这些现有的铁路基础设施都已经到位了。

sentences.en: Stuff like crossing gates and bells and signals for where the rails intersect the roads.
sentences.zh: 比如道口栏杆、铃铛以及铁轨与道路交叉处的信号灯等东西。

sentences.en: And that infrastructure is now used to stop traffic so rail bikes can cross.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些基础设施被用来拦截交通，以便铁轨单车通过。

sentences.en: It's kind of funny when you go through the railroad crossings and all the gates come down.
sentences.zh: 当你穿过铁路道口，所有的栏杆都降下来时，感觉有点搞笑。

sentences.en: And these rail bikes go past with us waving at the people in the cars.
sentences.zh: 这些铁轨单车从我们身旁驶过，我们向车里的人挥手。

sentences.en: That sounds amazing.
sentences.zh: 听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And of course, they vary in terms of legality, some being a little less illegal than others.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们的合法性各不相同，有些比别的稍微没那么违法。

sentences.en: But honestly, I would write any of them.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，我都想骑。

sentences.en: Attention passengers.
sentences.zh: 请注意，乘客们。

sentences.en: For those interested in taking home a train of their own, there are model trains in our onboard gift shop.
sentences.zh: 对于那些有兴趣把一列火车带回家的人，我们车上的礼品店里有模型火车。

sentences.en: Neil Young is best known for his music, but he also has a lesser known passion, model trainsets.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·杨以他的音乐最为著名，但他还有一个鲜为人知的爱好——模型火车套装。

sentences.en: He got his first one at age five.
sentences.zh: 他五岁时得到了第一套。

sentences.en: And throughout his years touring as a world famous musician, he built up a collection of vintage Lionel model trainsets.
sentences.zh: 在他作为世界著名音乐家到处巡演的多年里，他收藏了一批复古的莱昂内尔模型火车套装。

sentences.en: Neil's two sons, Zeke and Ben, were both born with cerebral palsy.
sentences.zh: 尼尔的两个儿子，齐克和本，都患有脑瘫。

sentences.en: In Ben's case, it rendered him quadriplegic and nonverbal.
sentences.zh: 就本而言，这导致他四肢瘫痪且无法说话。

sentences.en: Neil's then wife, Peggy, struggling to find good schools for children with disabilities, founded The Bridge School.
sentences.zh: 尼尔当时的妻子佩吉，在努力为残疾儿童寻找好学校时，创立了“大桥学校”。

sentences.en: In 1986, Neil found a unique way to engage with Ben through trains.
sentences.zh: 1986年，尼尔找到了通过火车与本互动的独特方式。

sentences.en: When I started building the railroad, I built it so that my son and I could have something to do together.
sentences.zh: 当我开始建造铁路线时，我建它是为了让我和儿子能一起做点事。

sentences.en: Neil extensively modified his vintage trains, adapting the controls to suit Ben's abilities.
sentences.zh: 尼尔对他的复古火车进行了大量改装，调整了控制系统以适应本的能力。

sentences.en: I developed a model train control system for Lionel and the sound systems because I basically made this for my kid so he could do it with his little switch.
sentences.zh: 我为莱昂内尔开发了一个模型火车控制系统和音响系统，因为我基本上是为我孩子制作的，这样他就能用自己的小开关来操作了。

sentences.en: But you're some kind of a mechanical, electronic, in addition to being musically...
sentences.zh: 但除了作为音乐家，你还是某种机械、电子……

sentences.en: Very nerdy, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，是个十足的书呆子。

sentences.en: He holds seven patents for his train innovations, including remote control and more realistic sounds.
sentences.zh: 他拥有七项关于火车创新的专利，包括远程控制和更逼真的声音。

sentences.en: He worked closely with Lionel in the early 1990s, and they incorporated his designs into the train master command control.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪90年代初与莱昂内尔紧密合作，他们将他的设计融入了火车大师指令控制系统。

sentences.en: Around the same time, Lionel faced bankruptcy, and Neil led a group of investors to bail them out.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，莱昂内尔面临破产，尼尔带领一群投资者对其进行了纾困。

sentences.en: Ben frequently accompanies his dad on tour.
sentences.zh: 本经常陪着他爸爸去巡演。

sentences.en: And these days, with the help of modern speech communication devices, runs a successful organic egg farm.
sentences.zh: 如今，在现代语音通信设备的帮助下，他经营着一家成功的有机鸡蛋农场。

sentences.en: In recent years, Neil has begun to sell off his vast model train collection.
sentences.zh: 近年来，尼尔开始出售他庞大的模型火车收藏。

sentences.en: In part, he wants others to find joy and connection through these vintage sets.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他希望其他人也能通过这些复古套装找到快乐和连接。

sentences.en: But he's also doing it for a good cause.
sentences.zh: 但他也为了一个崇高的事业。

sentences.en: He's donating the proceeds to The Bridge School to help other kids like Ben.
sentences.zh: 他将收益捐给大桥学校，以帮助像本这样的其他孩子。

sentences.en: Our next stop will be Mecca, Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 我们的下一站是沙特阿拉伯麦加。

sentences.en: Please note, this route is only operational until the end of the week.
sentences.zh: 请注意，这条路线仅运营至本周末。

sentences.en: So there's this train line that, for one week a year, has the highest reported capacity of any metro system in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一条铁路线，一年中有一周，其报告的客流量是全世界所有地铁系统中最高的。

sentences.en: But there's a caveat.
sentences.zh: 但有个附加条件。

sentences.en: It only operates for one week a year.
sentences.zh: 它一年只运营一周。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm hooked.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我被吸引了。

sentences.en: So why build a train that runs only one week a year?
sentences.zh: 那为什么要建造一条只运行一周的火车呢？

sentences.en: The network is based in Mecca.
sentences.zh: 这个网络设在麦加。

sentences.en: And the reason it only operates for this short annual period is that it's designed for a single purpose.
sentences.zh: 它之所以只在这个短期的年度期间运营，是因为它是为一个单一目的设计的。

sentences.en: Moving Muslims around the region during the Hajj.
sentences.zh: 在朝觐期间在该地区运送穆斯林。

sentences.en: Okay, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这说得通。

sentences.en: So pilgrims are traveling to Mecca.
sentences.zh: 所以朝圣者正在前往麦加。

sentences.en: They need to get between various holy sites.
sentences.zh: 他们需要在各个圣地之间穿梭。

sentences.en: And it's only a short time of the year.
sentences.zh: 而且一年中只有很短的一段时间。

sentences.en: With substantial increases in the number of pilgrims and vehicles carrying them in the holy sites,
sentences.zh: 随着圣地内朝圣者数量以及运送他们的车辆数量大幅增加，

sentences.en: the road network has become unable to accommodate pedestrians and vehicles simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 道路网络已经无法同时容纳行人和车辆。

sentences.en: So the whole region is notoriously crowded during holy week.
sentences.zh: 因此，在朝圣周期间，整个地区出了名的拥挤。

sentences.en: And people flood in during the Hajj.
sentences.zh: 人们在朝觐期间蜂拥而至。

sentences.en: Because one of the five pillars of Islam is visiting Mecca at least once in your lifetime.
sentences.zh: 因为伊斯兰教的五功之一就是在你的一生中至少去一次麦加。

sentences.en: At least for those who are able.
sentences.zh: 至少对于那些有能力的人来说。

sentences.en: And during this one narrow window of time each year.
sentences.zh: 而且是在每年这短短的一段时间窗口内。

sentences.en: So I know millions of people make the pilgrimage each year.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道每年有数百万人进行朝圣。

sentences.en: And I've read that things can get pretty crowded and dangerous, even deadly.
sentences.zh: 我读到过，情况会变得相当拥挤和危险，甚至是致命的。

sentences.en: Because when you have that many people, it can turn into a stampede pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 因为当你有这么多人时，非常容易演变成踩踏事件。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: The crowding has led to some really tragic deaths in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 过去，拥挤曾导致一些真正悲惨的死亡。

sentences.en: But there are other health risks too.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他健康风险。

sentences.en: The region gets super hot during the Hajj.
sentences.zh: 朝觐期间，该地区变得超级热。

sentences.en: So spending a lot of time outside, traveling between sites can be risky.
sentences.zh: 因此，花大量时间在户外、在各个圣地之间奔波可能会有风险。

sentences.en: Physical safety is definitely part of what drove this project.
sentences.zh: 身体安全绝对是推动这个项目的原因之一。

sentences.en: The government of the custodian of the two holy mosques decided to build a railway in the southern section of the holy sites.
sentences.zh: 两圣地监护人政府决定在圣地南部修建一条铁路。

sentences.en: The southern line, Upt al-Masha'ar al-Muqaddasa mitra, will be the most effective solution to transport the largest possible number of pilgrims in the shortest possible time.
sentences.zh: 南部线路，即麦沙尔朝圣地铁，将是在最短时间内运送最多朝圣者的最有效解决方案。

sentences.en: So, as you can imagine, back in the day, these pilgrims are traveling by camel or on foot.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以想象，过去这些朝圣者是骑骆驼或步行出行的。

sentences.en: And then when these roads came along, as any urbanist knows, they ironically led to more congestion, not less.
sentences.zh: 然后当这些道路出现时，正如任何城市规划者所知，具有讽刺意味的是，它们导致了更多的交通拥堵，而不是减少。

sentences.en: Especially with the rise of personal motor vehicles.
sentences.zh: 特别是随着个人机动车的兴起。

sentences.en: So in 2009, they started building this rail line.
sentences.zh: 所以在2009年，他们开始修建这条铁路线。

sentences.en: And the project employed thousands of engineers and even more construction workers who, in total, had to move nearly 200 million cubic meters of Earth.
sentences.zh: 该项目雇用了数千名工程师和更多的建筑工人，他们总共必须搬移近2亿立方米的泥土。

sentences.en: And despite that, the whole thing was completed in just two years, which is incredibly fast if you think about the scope.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，整个工程在短短两年内就完成了，如果考虑到它的规模，这快得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: And then in 2011, it carried nearly 4 million pilgrims around between these holy sites.
sentences.zh: 然后在2011年，它在这些圣地之间运送了近400万朝圣者。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that is hard to imagine, 4 million people being moved in a week.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难想象，一周内运送400万人。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And if you break it down even further, it can carry 70,000 people per hour, which I also have a hard time imagining, because it has trains leaving every few minutes.
sentences.zh: 如果你作进一步细分，它每小时可以运送70,000人，我也很难想象这一点，因为它每隔几分钟就有一班火车出发。

sentences.en: And in terms of what this offsets in terms of other traffic, they calculated that this train system replaces the need for over 50,000 surface buses, which, of course,
sentences.zh: 至于它在抵消其他交通方面起到的作用，他们计算出这个火车系统取代了对5万多辆地面公交的需求，当然，

sentences.en: helps reduce that congestion.
sentences.zh: 这有助于减少交通拥堵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But why, you know, if they put all this effort into it, why not just keep it open year-round just because, you know?
sentences.zh: 但是为什么，你知道的，如果他们付出了这么大的努力，为什么不直接全年开放呢，就因为，你知道的？

sentences.en: You know, I wasn't able to find a definitive official answer for that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我没能找到一个确切的官方答案。

sentences.en: My somewhat educated best guess is that it just isn't cost-efficient to operate it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我凭一些常识做出最好的猜测是，全天候运营它的成本效益不高。

sentences.en: And the route isn't really optimized for commuters or other everyday uses.
sentences.zh: 而且这条路线并没有真正针对通勤者或其他日常用途进行优化。

sentences.en: So it really, you know, only makes sense during the hajj.
sentences.zh: 所以它真的，你知道的，只在朝觐期间才有意义。

sentences.en: And the hajj, meanwhile, brings in so much money, it has almost certainly already offset the billions of dollars that the project costs, just to put that in perspective.
sentences.zh: 同时，朝觐带来了如此多的收入，它几乎可以肯定已经抵消了该项目耗资数十亿美元的成本，这么说吧。

sentences.en: So this one doesn't run regularly, but is there one optimized for commuting?
sentences.zh: 所以这条不定期运行，但有没有一条针对通勤进行优化的线路呢？

sentences.en: Like, is there an everyday metro system in the area?
sentences.zh: 比如说，该地区有没有日常的地铁系统？

sentences.en: Well, not yet, but they do have another network in the works that's supposed to serve the region more regularly and broadly, which, as I understand it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，还没有，但他们正在筹备另一个网络，旨在更定期、更广泛地服务该地区，据我所知，

sentences.en: won't even link up to this one.
sentences.zh: 它甚至不会与这条线路连接。

sentences.en: It'll just be a completely separate system.
sentences.zh: 它将是一个完全独立的系统。

sentences.en: And that'll be for more everyday use.
sentences.zh: 那将用于更多日常用途。

sentences.en: But this existing line is just going to continue being a once-a-year affair.
sentences.zh: 但现有的这条线路将继续是一年一次的事。

sentences.en: Attention passengers, do not be alarmed as this train is about to take to the sky, reach 88 miles per hour, and take us back to ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 请注意，乘客们，不要惊慌，因为这列火车即将腾空而起，时速达到88英里，带我们回到古罗马。

sentences.en: Enjoy the ride.
sentences.zh: 祝您旅途愉快。

sentences.en: There's some old infrastructure lore about the reason why American rails have such specific spacing.
sentences.zh: 有一些关于美国铁轨为什么会有如此特定间距的古老基础设施传说。

sentences.en: The persistent story is that American rail gauges, as in the distance between the metal rails,
sentences.zh: 流传的故事是，美国铁路轨距，也就是金属铁轨之间的距离，

sentences.en: can be directly traced all the way back to the wheel spacing of ancient imperial Roman chariots.
sentences.zh: 可以一直追溯到古代帝国罗马战车的车轮间距。

sentences.en: And the logic goes something like this.
sentences.zh: 其逻辑大致如下。

sentences.en: American rails are spaced four feet, eight and a half inches apart.
sentences.zh: 美国铁轨的间距是四英尺八点五英寸。

sentences.en: And that seemingly odd number comes from English spacing standards.
sentences.zh: 这个看似奇怪的数字来自英国的间距标准。

sentences.en: And those standards, in turn, were based on wagon construction dimensions.
sentences.zh: 而这些标准反过来又基于马车制造尺寸。

sentences.en: And those had to be standardized so wagons could ride in existing ruts.
sentences.zh: 这些尺寸必须标准化，以便马车能够在现有的车辙中行驶。

sentences.en: And those ruts were initially formed by the Roman Empire and reinforced by other vehicles ever since.
sentences.zh: 而这些车辙最初是由罗马帝国形成的，此后一直被其他车辆加固。

sentences.en: Now, there is some truth to this train of thought, but the legend itself, which has persisted for over a century, is mostly fanciful.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种想法确实有一点道理，但流传了一个多世纪的传说本身大多是虚构的。

sentences.en: For one thing, ancient Roman roads were built more for foot traffic than for chariots.
sentences.zh: 一方面，古代罗马道路的修建更多是为了步行交通，而不是为了战车。

sentences.en: Plus, current gauges were far from inevitable.
sentences.zh: 另外，当前的轨距远非不可避免。

sentences.en: For a long time, there was no standard gauge in the United States, and a variety were used.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，美国没有标准轨距，而是使用了各种各样的轨距。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the relative similarity between modern rail line gauges and ancient rutways are tied more to design than history.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，现代铁路线轨距与古代车辙之间的相对相似性更多地与设计有关，而不是历史。

sentences.en: Times may have changed, but the physical constraints of vehicles have remained relatively consistent.
sentences.zh: 时代可能变了，但车辆的物理限制保持了相对一致。

sentences.en: Axels need to span far enough to support the structure above them, but they can't be too wide or they might snap.
sentences.zh: 车轴需要跨度足够大以支撑其上方的结构，但又不能太宽，否则可能会断裂。

sentences.en: So, modern gauges aren't really a product of imperial Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以，现代轨距并不是帝国罗马的产物。

sentences.en: History rarely lets us trace such a direct line across such a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 历史很少让我们在如此漫长的时间跨度内追踪到这样一条直接的线索。

sentences.en: Still, it's also not entirely coincidental that rail spacing tends to fall into that certain range,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，铁轨间距倾向于落入那个特定范围内也不是完全巧合，

sentences.en: because the overall needs and limitations of ancient chariots and medieval wagons and contemporary railroads are broadly more similar than they are different.
sentences.zh: 因为古代战车、中世纪马车和当代铁路的总体需求和局限性，其相似之处远远多于不同之处。

sentences.en: Next stop, Anchorage, Alaska.
sentences.zh: 下一站，阿拉斯加安克雷奇。

sentences.en: If you wish to disembark before we arrive, please alert the conductor for a manual stop.
sentences.zh: 如果您希望在我们到达之前下车，请通知列车员进行手动停车。

sentences.en: Way up in Alaska, there's this one particular train that works differently from probably any train you've ever taken.
sentences.zh: 在遥远的阿拉斯加，有这样一列特殊的火车，它的运作方式可能与你坐过的任何火车都不同。

sentences.en: It operates on what's known as a flag stop basis.
sentences.zh: 它在所谓的“招手即停”基础上运营。

sentences.en: Okay, trains and flags.
sentences.zh: 好吧，火车和旗子。

sentences.en: All right, I'm on board.
sentences.zh: 行吧，我上车了。

sentences.en: Okay, so what does it mean for a rail line to operate on a flag stop basis?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么铁路线以“招手即停”的方式运营意味着什么？

sentences.en: What a flag stop train is, is basically a train that stops on demand when somebody needs to get off or get on.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“招手即停”火车，基本上是一列根据需要应要求停车的火车，当有人需要下车或上车时。

sentences.en: And there are some train routes that use a form of higher tech flag stop service, like they only slow down at a station if somebody's booked a ticket from there in advance, right?
sentences.zh: 有些铁路线路使用某种高科技的招手即停服务，比如只有当有人提前预订了那里的车票时，它们才会在车站减速，对吧？

sentences.en: Or in some parts of the world, there are these flag stop ferries where you have to flick a light switch on to get a boat's attention.
sentences.zh: 或者在世界的某些地方，有这种招手即停的渡轮，你必须按一下电灯开关来引起船只的注意。

sentences.en: But this kind of classic low-tech flag stop train where you literally wave a flag is very uncommon.
sentences.zh: 但这种经典的低技术含量、字面意义上挥舞旗帜的招手即停火车非常罕见。

sentences.en: And this route in Alaska is one of the last of its kind in North America.
sentences.zh: 这条阿拉斯加的路线是北美最后几条此类路线之一。

sentences.en: So how does the actual flagging down work?
sentences.zh: 那么实际的挥旗是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Like, do people just stand alongside the tracks, like in the dead of winter in Alaska, and just wave a white cloth around or maybe, you know, a scarf or whatever they have on them?
sentences.zh: 比如，人们就站在铁轨旁，就像在阿拉斯加数九寒冬里那样，然后挥舞一块白布，或者可能是，你知道的，一条围巾或他们身上有的任何东西？

sentences.en: Yeah, basically, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样的。

sentences.en: And the train operators are watching for those signals and stopping when they see them.
sentences.zh: 列车员会注意这些信号，并在看到信号时停车。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit more like a bus, but even buses have bus stops.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像公交车，但连公交车都有公交车站。

sentences.en: But what I don't get is, you know, the whole thing that makes a train great is that it efficiently moves on rails and has inertia.
sentences.zh: 但我不明白的是，你知道的，让火车伟大的整个原因在于它能在铁轨上高效运行并具有惯性。

sentences.en: And so how can you stop it to do these pickups when the pickups are done, you know, kind of spontaneously?
sentences.zh: 所以当这些上车需求是，你知道的，有点自发产生的时候，你又怎么能停下它来接客呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: I mean, these things have a ton of mass, but along this particular stretch, the trains are short.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这些东西的体量非常大，但在这一特定路段上，火车很短。

sentences.en: They only have two locomotives, two passenger cars and one baggage car.
sentences.zh: 它们只有两台机车、两节客车和一节行李车。

sentences.en: So they're small enough that they can start and stop a lot faster than a normal, you know, full-length locomotive and still achieve a maximum speed of close to 60 miles an hour.
sentences.zh: 所以它们体积很小，起步和停车比你知道的普通全长列车要快得多，同时最高时速还能接近每小时60英里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So if the trains are going up to 60 miles an hour, that means that it's a pretty rural area.
sentences.zh: 所以如果火车时速能达到60英里，那就说明这是一个相当偏远的地区。

sentences.en: So if that's the case, like, who are they stopping for?
sentences.zh: 既然如此，它们到底是在为谁停车呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, a lot of them are just visitors who are heading out to hike or fish in remote areas for maybe even a couple of weeks at a time,
sentences.zh: 对，很多乘客其实只是去偏远地区徒步或钓鱼的游客，有时甚至会待上一两周，

sentences.en: or they're traveling to their seasonal cabins.
sentences.zh: 或者他们是去自己季节性的木屋。

sentences.en: But the railway also provides a vital service for those brave, brave souls who live way out here in rural Alaska along this stretch.
sentences.zh: 但这条铁路也为那些勇敢无比、住在阿拉斯加偏远地区这片路段上的人们提供了一项至关重要的服务。

sentences.en: And it's been really interesting to see how this railroad provides a lifeline for the 40 or so people who live along here.
sentences.zh: 看到这条铁路如何为居住在这里的约40名居民提供生命线，真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: Just hang out a flag if you want the train to stop.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让火车停下，只要挂起一面旗子就行了。

sentences.en: And they stop and they pick you up or they drop you off wherever you're asking the conductor to stop.
sentences.zh: 它们会停下来接你，或者按照你要求售票员停车的地方把你放下。

sentences.en: So some folks use the train to get to and from their homes in the region, and they also need this train to get supply drops.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些当地人利用火车往返于他们在该地区的家，他们还需要这趟列车来运送物资。

sentences.en: But probably my favorite service they offer is news delivery, which doesn't actually require them to stop at all.
sentences.zh: 不过我最喜欢的服务可能还是投递新闻，这实际上根本不需要它们停车。

sentences.en: Basically, there's this rail worker who stands there and tosses out print newspapers for area residents from the moving train.
sentences.zh: 基本上，会有一名铁路工人在行驶中的火车上站着，把纸质报纸扔给当地居民。

sentences.en: They can even get their daily news, courtesy of Harry Ross.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至能靠哈里·罗斯享受到每日新闻的便利。

sentences.en: The people will come out, they'll send their dog out to come and pick up that newspaper, and the dog will bring it back to the cabin.
sentences.zh: 人们会出来，把狗派出去捡那份报纸，然后狗会把它带回木屋。

sentences.en: We have more trains, more Kurt Kolstad, and even more Alaska after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们还有更多关于火车的内容、更多库尔特·科尔斯特德，甚至还有更多的阿拉斯加。

sentences.en: Next stop, Wales, Alaska.
sentences.zh: 下一站，阿拉斯加威尔士。

sentences.en: This will be our final stop of the day, as the proposed tunnel that would take us to Russia has yet to be constructed.
sentences.zh: 这将是我们今天的最后一站，因为通往俄罗斯的拟议隧道尚未修建。

sentences.en: So, Kurt, we're still in Alaska?
sentences.zh: 所以，库尔特，我们还在阿拉斯加吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: We're still in Alaska.
sentences.zh: 我们还在阿拉斯加。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a really, really big state.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常非常大的州。

sentences.en: It's a huge state, and things are pretty spread out, which makes sense that there would be trains between them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的州，各地的距离相当分散，因此它们之间有火车也就说得通了。

sentences.en: But in this case, it's not a real train, or at least not yet.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，这不是一辆真正的火车，至少现在还不是。

sentences.en: For over a century, there have been various proposals to connect eastern Russia and Alaska across the Bering Strait,
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪以来，一直有各种跨越白令海峡连接俄罗斯东部和阿拉斯加的提议，

sentences.en: a project that would have to span a bit over 50 miles and would tie North America to Asia in this unprecedented way.
sentences.zh: 这个项目跨度将略超50英里，将以这种前所未有的方式把北美和亚洲联系起来。

sentences.en: Of course, in the current political climate, it's probably more of a pipe dream, but it would be a world-changing feat of engineering.
sentences.zh: 当然，在当前的政治气候下，这可能更像是一个不切实际的幻想，但这将是一项改变世界的工程壮举。

sentences.en: Such a tunnel would have major benefits.
sentences.zh: 这样的隧道将带来重大益处。

sentences.en: First of all, it would physically link North and South America to the old world.
sentences.zh: 首先，它将把南北美洲与旧大陆在物理上连接起来。

sentences.en: You could ride by train from San Francisco to Beijing in a day and a half,
sentences.zh: 你可以坐一天半的火车从旧金山到北京，

sentences.en: and travel by land all the way from Cape Town to Miami.
sentences.zh: 并且一路通过陆路从开普敦旅行到迈阿密。

sentences.en: A tunnel would provide a safer, cheaper, and faster way to transport freight between Asia and North America.
sentences.zh: 隧道将为亚洲和北美之间运输货物提供一条更安全、更便宜、更快速的途径。

sentences.en: Of course, right now, Russia is the aggressor in a needless and horrible war.
sentences.zh: 当然，就目前而言，俄罗斯是一场毫无必要且可怕的战争中的侵略者。

sentences.en: But putting geopolitics aside, at 50-plus miles, this sounds like a massive undertaking.
sentences.zh: 但抛开地平政治不谈，全长50多英里，这听起来像是一项庞大的工程。

sentences.en: I can imagine some pretty massive economic benefits for international trade, you know, if things were to work out diplomatically.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，如果外交上一切顺利的话，它会为国际贸易带来相当巨大的经济效益。

sentences.en: But are these just pine-in-the-sky ideas, or are people, like, really taking this seriously?
sentences.zh: 但这些只是空中楼阁式的想法，还是真的有人在认真对待？

sentences.en: Well, definitely some people have, including some pretty serious folks who've pitched plans for over a century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然有些人是认真的，包括一些相当严肃的人，他们在一个多世纪里一直在提出规划方案。

sentences.en: For example, you have Joseph Strauss, who went on to design something like 400 bridges,
sentences.zh: 例如，约瑟夫·斯特劳斯曾设计过大约400座桥梁，

sentences.en: and was the project engineer for the Golden Gate Bridge.
sentences.zh: 并且是金门大桥的项目工程师。

sentences.en: And he did his undergrad thesis on a Bering Strait bridge.
sentences.zh: 他的本科毕业论文写的就是白令海峡大桥。

sentences.en: Then, in 1905, a more fully fleshed-out plan was all but approved, but got axed at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1905年，一个更加成熟的方案几乎获得了批准，但却在最后一刻被否决了。

sentences.en: I mean, if they could build something as beautiful as the Golden Gate Bridge, but 50 miles long, that would be pretty stunning.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果他们能建造出像金门大桥那样美丽、但长达50英里的建筑，那将是非常震撼的。

sentences.en: I mean, what was the thing that killed the project back in 1905?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当年究竟是什么杀死了1905年的那个项目？

sentences.en: Well, the timing, as it turned out, was terrible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，时机太糟糕了。

sentences.en: The Russian Revolution was kicking off, so, you know, Tsar Nicholas II had bigger fish to fry.
sentences.zh: 当时俄国革命正在爆发，所以尼古拉二世沙皇有更重要的事情要处理。

sentences.en: And, you know, the next thing you know, everybody's caught up in World War I, and then that, you know, bleeds into World War II,
sentences.zh: 而且，你懂的，紧接着每个人都被卷入了第一次世界大战，然后你知道的，那又延续到了第二次世界大战，

sentences.en: and tensions were just high throughout.
sentences.zh: 而且整个期间局势一直很紧张。

sentences.en: So the idea kept getting shelved.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法不断被搁置。

sentences.en: And then in the 1950s, people started to ramp up and pitch various bridge and tunnel plans again,
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪50年代，人们开始重新积极筹划各种桥梁和隧道方案，

sentences.en: but none of them panned out, in part because of feasibility concerns, but also, of course, the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 但其中没有一个取得成功，部分原因是可行性方面的担忧，当然还有冷战的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I mean, I could just imagine it being a tough sell because there's the engineering challenge of doing something that massive in any climate,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以想象这很难推销，因为在任何气候下做如此大规模的事情都存在工程挑战，

sentences.en: and then you think about where they are in the world and connecting the Bering Strait.
sentences.zh: 然后你还要考虑到它们在世界上的地理位置以及连接白令海峡。

sentences.en: It's super cold.
sentences.zh: 那里超级冷。

sentences.en: The waters are very turbulent.
sentences.zh: 水流非常湍流。

sentences.en: And there's not a whole lot on either side of these things, you know, directly.
sentences.zh: 而且这些东西的任何一侧，你知道的，直接周边并没有太多东西。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, there's basically nothing, especially at the points that are closest to each other from, like, these nations.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，基本上什么都没有，特别是从这些国家来看彼此距离最近的点上。

sentences.en: And if they built a bridge, it would probably also have to be closed down for much of the year because it is so cold up there.
sentences.zh: 如果他们建造一座桥，它可能也必须在一年中的大部分时间里关闭，因为那里实在太冷了。

sentences.en: And if they went the train route, they'd need to figure out how to reconcile these different gauges for each country.
sentences.zh: 如果他们走铁路路线，他们就需要弄清楚如何协调每个国家这些不同的轨距。

sentences.en: And if they went the tunnel route, well, a 50-mile tunnel would be an incredible undertaking and would set a world record.
sentences.zh: 如果他们走隧道路线，好吧，一条50英里的隧道将是一项令人难以置信的工程，并将创造世界纪录。

sentences.en: So with all these obstacles and all these really logical reasons why it doesn't exist, is there any realistic prospect of this happening?
sentences.zh: 因此，面对所有这些障碍以及它不复存在的种种合乎逻辑的原因，这件事情还有任何现实的实现前景吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know for sure, but I was kind of stunned to find that about a decade ago, the Kremlin approved a rail tunnel proposal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我无法百分之百确定，但我惊讶地发现，大约十年前，克里姆林宫批准了一项铁路隧道提案。

sentences.en: Since 2007, the concept has advanced.
sentences.zh: 自2007年以来，这个概念一直在推进。

sentences.en: In 2008, Vladimir Putin, the then prime minister of Russia, approved the TKM link.
sentences.zh: 2008年，时任俄罗斯总理的弗拉基米尔·普京批准了TKM连接项目。

sentences.en: Then in August 2011, the Russian government approved the project.
sentences.zh: 然后，在2011年8月，俄罗斯政府批准了该项目。

sentences.en: So honestly, it seems like a really cool project.
sentences.zh: 所以老实说，这看起来是一个非常酷的项目。

sentences.en: But of course, this ongoing conflict between these two countries makes it really unlikely we're going to see any progress on this project, you know,
sentences.zh: 但当然，这两个国家之间持续的冲突使得我们真的很可能看不到这个项目取得任何进展，你知道的，

sentences.en: under the current Russian regime anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，在当前的俄罗斯政权下是这样的。

sentences.en: But given how persistent the idea has been to date, I would be shocked if it didn't resurface again someday.
sentences.zh: 但鉴于这个想法迄今为止表现出的执着，如果它有朝一日再次浮出水面，我会感到震惊。

sentences.en: I would not be shocked if it resurfaced again.
sentences.zh: 如果它再次浮出水面，我一点也不会感到震惊。

sentences.en: And then when you lay out the fact that this is going to be a decades-long project to actually complete,
sentences.zh: 当你陈述这个事实——即这将是一个历时数十年才能最终完成的项目时，

sentences.en: it is hard to imagine political stability that would persist through the actual construction of such a project.
sentences.zh: 很难想象会有什么样的政治稳定能够在一个实际历经如此项目的建设过程中持续存在。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, getting that handshake to last for decades seems kind of like an impossible task given the history between our countries.
sentences.zh: 对，鉴于我们两国之间的历史，要让那种握手维持几十年，听起来像是不可能的任务。

sentences.en: But here's hoping.
sentences.zh: 不过还是抱有希望吧。

sentences.en: It would be so cool to see it, though.
sentences.zh: 不过能看到它真的会很酷。

sentences.en: It would be amazing.
sentences.zh: 那将是惊人的。

sentences.en: It would be cool.
sentences.zh: 那会很酷。

sentences.en: I would drive all the way through Alaska just to get to the bridge.
sentences.zh: 我愿意一路开车穿过阿拉斯加只为了到达那座桥。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Kurt.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，库尔特。

sentences.en: This was a great collection of trains again.
sentences.zh: 这又是一期关于火车的精彩合集。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Anytime, Roman.
sentences.zh: 随时奉陪，罗曼。

sentences.en: And if you're down for round three, I've got more ideas where these came from.
sentences.zh: 如果你准备好进行第三轮，我这里还有更多类似的点子。

sentences.en: I know you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你有。

sentences.en: It's so good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Thank you for riding with 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 感谢您与《99%无形》同行。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Kurt Kolstad, Martin Gonzalez, and Jacob Maldonado-Medina.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由库尔特·科尔斯特德、马丁·冈萨雷斯和雅各布·马尔多纳多-梅迪纳制作。

sentences.zh: 克里斯·伯鲁贝是我们值得信赖的列车长。

sentences.zh: 音乐由音响总监斯旺·里阿尔创作，米亚·伯恩担任吉他手和夏威夷吉他手。

sentences.zh: 德兰妮·霍尔是高级编辑。

sentences.zh: 团队其他成员包括薇薇安·莱、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、杰森·德莱昂、克里斯托弗·约翰逊、

sentences.zh: 拉什·马登、乔·罗森伯格、凯利·普赖恩、索菲亚·克拉茨克、实习生奥利维亚·格林，还有我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.zh: 我们是 Stitcher 和 Sirius XM 播客家族的一部分，总部现在位于加利福尼亚州美丽的奥克兰市中心北部六个街区的潘多拉大厦。
